title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is re-deriving Lagrange's integration of dx/√X = dy/√Y, where X = A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ and Y is the same quartic in y. This is the Euler addition theorem for elliptic integrals. Euler's own earlier proofs reached it by guessing a symmetric biquadratic relation; Lagrange's 1766–69 method instead derives it.

Setup (previous page): introduce an auxiliary time t with dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = √Y. Put p = x+y and q = x−y.
- Then dp·dq/dt² = X−Y = q[B + Cp + ¼D(3p²+q²) + ½Ep(p²+q²)].
- Differentiating x′² = X and y′² = Y gives x″ = X′/2 and y″ = Y′/2.

On this page:
1. p″ = ½(X′+Y′) = B + Cp + ¾D(p²+q²) + ½Ep(p²+3q²).
2. Subtracting p′q′/q leaves p″ − p′q′/q = ½Dq² + Epq². This is the key cancellation: B and C drop out.
3. Dividing by q² gives (p″/q² − p′q′/q³) = ½D + Ep.
4. Multiplying by 2p′ makes the left side the exact derivative d/dt(p′²/q²). Integrating gives p′²/q² = Δ + Dp + Ep², with Δ an arbitrary constant.
5. Since p′ = √X+√Y, this yields Lagrange's algebraic integral (√X+√Y)/(x−y) = √(Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)²).

§39 begins rationalising it.
- Squaring gives (X+Y+2√XY)/(x−y)² = Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)².
- Subtract (D(x+y)+E(x+y)²)(x−y)² from X+Y. This uses x³+y³ − (x+y)(x−y)² = xy(x+y) and x⁴+y⁴ − (x²−y²)² = 2x²y².
- What remains is 2A + B(x+y) + C(x²+y²) + Dxy(x+y) + 2Ex²y².

The next page completes this to the symmetric biquadratic form (2A + B(x+y) + 2Cxy + Dxy(x+y) + 2Ex²y² + 2√XY)/(x−y)² = Γ, Euler's classical form of the addition theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; all coefficient computations check: ¾ and ½ for the p″ formula, ½Dq² + Epq² for the difference, and xy(x+y) and 2x²y² in §39.

Neighbouring-page transcription: in §36 the formula after dividing by q should read ½Ep(pp+qq), not ½Epq(pp+qq). With the correct form the subtraction on this page works, so this is a transcription (or possibly printing) slip.
Previous page §37: 'dX = Y′dy' should be 'dY = Y′dy'.
Implicit sign choice: both differentials are set equal to +dt. The other branch (√X − √Y) is covered only through the arbitrary constant and the squaring later; Euler does not discuss this.

ideas.what: Introducing an auxiliary 'time' t so that the separated equation becomes a mechanical-type second-order system in p = x+y and q = x−y, followed by finding a first integral.
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's dynamical method for the elliptic addition theorem (reduction to an integrable ODE system)
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1780, publ. 1784); exposition of Lagrange's method

ideas.what: Cancellation of B and C in p″ − p′q′/q, giving an equation that becomes exact after division by q² and multiplication by 2p′.
Algebraic integral (√X+√Y)/(x−y) = √(Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)²) and its reduction to the symmetric biquadratic form.
ideas.modern_name: Euler addition theorem for elliptic integrals (general quartic)
ideas.where_published: E251, E252, E261 (Institutiones calculi integralis I) and E506

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, correct, and well-known exposition of Lagrange's published method, linking it to Euler's own canonical biquadratic integral. Nothing here is absent from the standard historical accounts of the addition theorem.
